pr_title: Reduce verbosity of the bulk indexing audit log
pr_comments: Hi @albertzaharovits, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

> I wonder if it makes sense to add a new field item_count or similar to indicate how many items there were.

Good question. I haven't considered it before.

Considering it now, I don't think it's worth it really. The number of bulk items in requests is not informative, as it doesn't reflect the number of "touched" docs, because multiple items can affect a single doc id. Plus, the count of doc "touches" is split across multiple shard requests, possibly across multiple node's audits, so it can even get to be misleading.
Even more, this borders on exposing information from the request body contents, which we only do in specific cases (specific actions that change security configuration), and that means we don't have a good audit field naming convention to expose such summary information on the request body.

The only "pro" argument is that previously `"request.name":"BulkItemRequest"` type-of requests really did stand in for a single bulk item, but now they stand for multiples (essentially collating identical entries into a single one), and there's no indication for this collation.

I'm leaning on not adding it, though it can easily be added if anybody complains about it (but it's harder to take it away).
